title: Latency-aware pulse release controller for canary rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a new 'pulse' release controller that advances traffic to a candidate model in short, repeatable pulses. Each pulse size and cadence adapts to live latency and quality signals (p99 latency, error rate, model-eval delta). The controller integrates shadow probes and A/B gating and supports automated soft rollback steps before full rollback to minimize user disruption.
background: Current canary primitives use fixed step schedules or percentage ramps that do not react to sudden shifts in latency or model quality. We see several incidents where models introduced small but sharp p99 regressions that required manual rollback. The goal here is an SLO-first pacing approach that performs small, measurable exposures (pulses), evaluates telemetry during hold windows, and either proceeds, shrinks the next pulse, pauses, or performs a staged rollback.
goals: Design a policy controller that drives canary progress by discrete pulses rather than continuous ramps
Use real-time SLO and model-eval signals to adjust pulse size and inter-pulse delay
Support shadow probing and A/B routes for high-risk cohorts during pulse windows
Implement auto-escalation rollback: soft-step back (reduce weight) then full rollback if persistent regressions
Provide clear telemetry and console UX for pulse state, decision reasons, and manual overrides
non_goals: Replace existing rollout DSL immediately — this will be an opt-in controller with a new policy type
Handle multi-region cross-traffic reconciliation in v1 (region-aware routing will be follow-up)
Perform model parameter changes or automated retraining as part of rollback
acceptance_criteria: Controller can be configured via Console and API with a pulse schedule and SLO thresholds
In integration tests, controller advances candidate in pulses and adapts pulse sizes when p99 latency crosses thresholds
Shadow probes are emitted and recorded in telemetry for at least one pulse per rollout
Auto soft-rollback (reduce candidate weight by N steps) triggers on defined metric breach and is reversible via manual override
Console UI surfaces last decision reason and per-pulse metrics for at least 30 days
rollout_policy_dsl:
# Example policy (YAML-like)
policy_type: pulse_release
base_pulse: 0.5%
max_pulse: 10%
initial_hold: 60s
max_hold: 10m
pulse_growth: adaptive  # growth is adjusted based on signals
signals:
  - name: p99_latency_ms
    threshold: 600
    direction: higher_is_bad
  - name: error_rate
    threshold: 0.01
    direction: higher_is_bad
  - name: model_eval_delta_score
    threshold: -0.02
    direction: lower_is_bad
actions:
  breach: soft_rollback  # scale candidate weight down by last_pulse or pause
  repeated_breach: full_rollback
shadow_probe: enabled
ab_tests: allow_cohort_override
metrics_window: rolling_5m
implementation_notes: Controller implemented as a new rollout driver in the orchestration layer with a small state machine: Idle -> EmitPulse -> Hold -> Evaluate -> Decide
Use existing telemetry sinks (console metrics, traces, and runtime-telemetry) to compute pulse-level aggregates
Leverage prefix/KV cache compatibility checks to ensure candidate variant can serve probe traffic without cold-start penalty
Expose controller decisions and candidate weight history via the rollout events API for audit/logging
Provide a feature flag to enable circuit-breaker mode that forces immediate full rollback for P0 incidents
telemetry_and_observability: New per-pulse metric namespace: rollout.pulse.{rollout_id}.{pulse_id} with counts, p50/p90/p99, error_rate, eval_delta
Decision reason tag included on every pulse event (e.g., 'growth_ok', 'p99_breach', 'shadow_mismatch')
Console timeline view: pulse markers, metric overlays, and ability to replay decisions for a selected window
Alert rules: immediate paging for repeated_breach leading to full_rollback; warning alerts for single pulse soft_rollback
testing_plan: Unit tests for state machine transitions with mocked signals
Integration tests in staging with traffic replay that simulates latency spikes and model-eval regressions
Chaos test: inject gradual latency increase and verify controller pauses or performs soft rollback instead of continuing
End-to-end test against console: create rollout, observe pulses, simulate breach, confirm auto-rollback behavior
Load test to validate controller scales with 1k concurrent rollouts (simulated)
migration_plan: Phase 1: add controller behind opt-in feature flag; only new rollouts can select pulse_release policy
Phase 2: add console UI controls, safe defaults, and documentation; run internal dogfooding for 2 weeks
Phase 3: open opt-in to customers and collect feedback; keep classic ramp policy as fallback
Phase 4: evaluate telemetry and if stable, propose promoted policy as recommended default
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: overly aggressive growth may expose users — mitigation: conservative default base_pulse (0.5%) and upper bound enforcement
Risk: noisy signals causing oscillation — mitigation: require multiple consecutive pulses of breach before full_rollback; use hysteresis windows
Risk: increased complexity for operators — mitigation: clear console decision reasons, explainable logs, and one-click rollback
Risk: probe traffic affecting bill/cost — mitigation: default probes limited to 0.1% traffic and adjustable by policy
